Briefing for 12 November 2026

Short items for 12 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

Everyday tool

Claude adds spreadsheets, whiteboards and meetings

Anthropic launched Claude Sheets and Claude Whiteboards in beta and made dashboards generally available as Claude Data. Claude Meetings, a beta for Team and Enterprise, lets Claude join Google Meet calls and start tasks.

Source: Anthropic

Everyday tool

Gemini now talks with you in Apple CarPlay

Google is rolling out a Gemini app for Apple CarPlay worldwide. iPhone users can hold hands-free voice conversations while driving, for example to catch up on email or prepare for a meeting.

Source: Google

New model

Alibaba opens a short preview of Qwen4-Max

Alibaba released Qwen4-Max-Preview, a new flagship model for text, image and video understanding, reasoning and tool use. The preview runs only through its Token Plan and is scheduled to end on November 25.

Source: Alibaba Cloud

New model

AlphaGenome 2 predicts DNA effects per cell type

Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 estimates how genetic variants change gene activity in hundreds of human cell types. It is open to non-commercial research and is not meant for clinical diagnosis.

Source: Google DeepMind

New model

Runway releases its robot model Praxis-1 openly

Runway published weights and code for Praxis-1, a world action model for robot arms, under the Apache 2.0 license. Robotics teams can now run and adapt it on their own hardware.

Source: Runway

In the background

OpenAI can stop research models within 35 seconds

OpenAI described Control Room, a central system that tracks model jobs across its research infrastructure. Once staff decide to intervene, it halts a job's model output within 35 seconds.

Source: OpenAI

In the background

New York opens registration for big AI labs

Under the RAISE Act, large frontier AI developers must register with New York by January 1, 2027. From then on they must publish safety frameworks and report critical safety incidents within 72 hours.

Source: New York State

AI agents

United won't let AI agents book flights

United Airlines is restricting third-party AI agents on its booking platforms, citing data security and regulation. Assistants may still show flight options, but customers have to complete the purchase themselves.

Source: CNBC

Be brave. Get smart.
